text: Pick one task, give it full focus, then stop. Did the outcome actually need more?
What outcome am I actually trying to create here? Do I need to do this, or just need the result?
Think of a recent win. Was it the hours you put in, or the thinking and timing?
Before adding this: would removing a task move you forward faster than adding one?
Did you need the full session, or could you have moved on sooner?
If you could only finish one thing today, which task would actually move the needle? Start there.
Busyness feels like progress. But which of yesterday's tasks actually changed an outcome?
You just finished a focused block. Before starting the next: is continuing the highest-value move right now?
Your list has weight. Each item costs attention even when you're not on it. Does this one earn its place?
What if today's work is already enough? What would you do with the rest of the day?
Some of your best results came from less effort, not more. What made those different?
Is this genuinely urgent, or does it just feel that way? Urgency and importance are different signals.
How was the quality of your attention in that session? One focused hour often beats three scattered ones.
For each task: do it, delegate it, or drop it. Two of those three don't need your time.
